definition: A Transmission System Operator (TSO) manages a power grid; when it is unaffiliated with local government it is called an Independent System Operator (ISO); an ISO whose footprint crosses state lines is also called a Regional Transmission Operator (RTO).
core_idea: TSO is the generic term for any grid operator, while ISO/RTO describe operators running deregulated, free-trading grids, with RTO specifically denoting multi-state coverage.
key_points: TSOs are sometimes run directly by local governments
An ISO is a TSO independent of local government
An RTO is an ISO whose grid spans multiple states
Most electricity trading happens on RTO/ISO-run deregulated grids
The book uses 'TSO' generically for any grid operator and 'RTO/ISO' for deregulated-market operators
relationships: ERCOT functions as this kind of grid operator
trading_implications: Grid operator type/affiliation signals how much local-government vs market-based rule-making governs trading
caveats: ISO and RTO are sometimes used loosely; RTO specifically implies crossing state boundaries
